suppress.notes: kotlin-stdlib-common cannot be bumped past 1.9.25: as of 2.4.20 it is a packaging=pom artifact with no published jar (confirmed via Maven Central), so no fixed jar exists for it to resolve to. The underlying reachability argument from the original suppression above still applies unchanged: the vulnerable code path is Kotlin's incremental-compilation build-cache deserialization, never exercised by BrewDeck's Maven build.

WebFlux-only (PartEventHttpMessageReader / multipart handling). BrewDeck has no spring-webflux on the classpath (Spring MVC + Tomcat only, confirmed via `mvn dependency:tree`); this code path does not exist in the application.

Requires an application-defined org.springframework.web.servlet.view.xslt.XsltView (or XsltViewResolver) plus a "/**" catch-all mapping that renders a view without an explicit view name. BrewDeck has no template engine (no Thymeleaf/FreeMarker/ Mustache dependency), no ViewResolver configuration, and every endpoint is a @RestController returning JSON directly - XsltView is never constructed.

WebFlux functional endpoints deployed atop DispatcherServlet. BrewDeck has no spring-webflux on the classpath and defines no RouterFunction-based endpoints - every endpoint is annotation-based (@RestController/@RequestMapping).

WebFlux applications parsing XML via the Aalto processor. BrewDeck has no spring-webflux and no com.fasterxml:aalto-xml anywhere in the resolved dependency tree (confirmed via `mvn dependency:tree`); this reader is never instantiated.

WebFlux WebSocket support. BrewDeck has no spring-webflux on the classpath and no WebSocket endpoints in src/main/java (confirmed via source grep); the tomcat-embed-websocket jar present is Tomcat's own servlet-based WebSocket container, bundled by default but never used to open an endpoint, and is unrelated to WebFlux's reactive WebSocket stack targeted by this advisory.

Spring MVC's "functional web framework" (RouterFunction-based endpoints) combined with Server-Sent Events. BrewDeck defines zero RouterFunction/functional endpoints (confirmed via source grep) and no SseEmitter/text-event-stream usage - every endpoint is annotation-based and returns a plain JSON response body.

Requires Server-Sent Events combined with server-side "view fragments" (a template-engine rendering feature, e.g. Thymeleaf fragments streamed via SSE). BrewDeck has no template engine dependency, no ViewResolver, and no SSE endpoints anywhere in src/main/java - it is a JSON-only REST API.

WebFlux running on the Jetty 12 Core reactive server adapter. BrewDeck has no spring-webflux and no Eclipse Jetty dependency anywhere in the resolved tree (confirmed via `mvn dependency:tree`); the application runs on the default embedded Tomcat servlet container via spring-boot-starter-web.

Spring RSocket support. BrewDeck has no io.rsocket dependency, no spring-boot-starter-rsocket, and no reactor-netty anywhere in the resolved dependency tree (confirmed via `mvn dependency:tree`); no RSocket server or client is configured.

Requires an application to evaluate user-supplied Spring Expression Language (SpEL) text at runtime (e.g. via ExpressionParser/SpelExpressionParser). A full source grep of src/main/java found zero SpEL evaluation, zero @PreAuthorize/@PostAuthorize/@PreFilter/@PostFilter method-security annotations, and no template engine (Thymeleaf's view layer is the other common SpEL entry point) - BrewDeck never parses or evaluates a SpEL expression, user-supplied or otherwise.

Same SpEL-evaluation prerequisite as CVE-2026-47886 above (SimpleEvaluationContext is a SpEL API): BrewDeck never constructs an EvaluationContext or evaluates a SpEL expression anywhere in src/main/java (confirmed via source grep). No method security annotations, no template engine, no dynamic expression evaluation.

Spring Security's embedded WebAuthn support with a distributed HTTP session store. BrewDeck uses stateless JWT authentication (no HTTP session store at all) and has no WebAuthn configuration, dependency, or endpoint anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via source grep).

Spring Security's embedded UnboundID test LDAP server (UnboundIdContainer). BrewDeck has no org.springframework.security:spring-security-ldap dependency and no UnboundIdContainer bean anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via `mvn dependency:tree` and source grep); authentication is JWT/BCrypt-based against PostgreSQL, not LDAP.
